q: What is the default throttle limit for API Gateway and how does it compare to Lambda's default concurrency?

opts.a: API Gateway: 5,000 RPS, Lambda: 500 concurrent executions
opts.b: API Gateway: 10,000 RPS, Lambda: 1,000 concurrent executions
opts.c: API Gateway: 10,000 RPS, Lambda: 10,000 concurrent executions
opts.d: API Gateway: 1,000 RPS, Lambda: 1,000 concurrent executions

exp.a: Incorrect. These are not the correct default values.
exp.b: Correct. API Gateway has a default throttle limit of 10,000 requests per second, whereas Lambda has a default concurrency limit of 1,000. This mismatch can cause throttling issues [1].
exp.c: Incorrect. Lambda's default concurrency is 1,000, not 10,000.
exp.d: Incorrect. API Gateway's default is 10,000, not 1,000.

q: A team deployed an application using API Gateway and Lambda. Under heavy load, Lambda functions start getting throttled while API Gateway continues accepting requests. What causes this issue?

opts.a: API Gateway timeout is too short

opts.d: API Gateway payload size is too large

exp.a: Incorrect. Timeout doesn't cause throttling.
exp.b: Correct. API Gateway's default throttle limit of 10,000 RPS can overwhelm Lambda's default 1,000 concurrent execution limit, causing throttling [1].
exp.c: Incorrect. Memory doesn't affect concurrency limits.
exp.d: Incorrect. Payload size is unrelated to throttling.
